elliptical_recognition_followup.note: Native replay of the unchanged retained evidence. Top-level counts and original notes describe the original circular-only checkpoint; this follow-up is not a new Rhino run.

notes: Owned private Xvfb Rhino session, public APIs and actual SplitEdge component/point clicks. No existing Rhino session or user desktop was targeted.

A first attempt stopped at a missing shared artifact after open-profile extrusion preparation failed. The arc source was corrected to a natural surface face, artifact preparation was verified, and a complete 30-case diagnostic preceded the final fresh 44-case run retained here.
Portable inputs omit only shared B-rep artifact paths. Raw response JSON is compacted without numerical normalization or array reordering.

Each family tests one-shot Cen over five persistent modes and persistent Cen alone. Actual point-prompt matrices, public WorldToClient coordinates and integer clicks are retained; replay uses a 12-pixel capture radius.

Thirty-four independently computed native centers drive full ordered geometry/attribute/selection/history comparison at absolute 1e-9 and relative 1e-10. No recorded Rhino result point is supplied to native capture.
Empty-center and outside-arc controls are admission-only misses. Outside-arc clicks fail to split and therefore do not perform Undo/Redo.

Rhino captures the ellipse at x=4 and the perturbed quadratic elliptic arc at x=3.75. Their original declared x=4 hypotheses remain unchanged. Native circular recognition rejects both noncircular loci; these four records are known limits, not matches.

The all-negative homogeneous gauge is the same circular locus and is recognized natively, while Rhino misses it in both modes. This difference is retained rather than reproducing the recognition failure.

SplitEdge constrains a point to the selected edge. These are not direct unconstrained GetPoint observations and do not establish depth/occlusion preference between projected coincident circular boundaries.
